summary:

title: Rinvoq Becomes First Pill Approved for Nonsegmental Vitiligo After About 1 in 4 Regained Most Facial Color
summary:
The FDA has approved Rinvoq (upadacitinib), AbbVie's once-daily pill, for nonsegmental vitiligo in adults and adolescents 12 and older. It is the first systemic treatment for the condition in the United States, meaning a medicine that works throughout the body rather than only on the skin. AbbVie announced the approval on Nov. 23, and the approved dose is 15 milligrams a day, AJMC reported.

title: FDA Approves First Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Drug
summary:
## FACTS

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Monday, Nov. 23, approved Welgemda (ribitol) to treat limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, a rare inherited muscle disease, according to an FDA news release. “Welgemda is the first therapy approved for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy,” the agency said. The oral drug is made by ML Bio Solutions and distributed by BridgeBio Pharma, and it is approved for adults and children who weigh at least 30 kilograms, or about 66 pounds.

title: Ekitna Plus Sunitinib Wins FDA Approval for Advanced GIST After Nearly Doubling Time Before Cancer Progression
summary:
The FDA on Nov. 24 approved Ekitna (bezuclastinib), from Cogent Biosciences, for use with sunitinib in adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors, or GIST, who have already been treated with imatinib, according to the FDA announcement.

In the phase 3 PEAK trial, people taking the combination went a median of 16.5 months before their cancer grew, compared with 9.2 months on sunitinib alone. Overall survival data are not yet mature, so it is not known whether patients will live longer.
